setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the example MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. Nothing is assigned to Trig params yet, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open Trig params (E1 to the channel's Trig params page), press K2 to enter the slot list, turn E3 until the parameter reads Chord Note Strum, press K3 to assign it to the first slot, then press K2 to leave the list. The slot shows as Strm on the screen: it is the strum slot.
steps.title: Give Chord Note Strum a slot

steps.caption: Press K3 to select the Strm slot. It reads X, which means no strum: the notes of a chord sound together. Every strum division is chosen with E3 from here.
steps.title: A new slot starts at X

steps.caption: Turn E3 left a few detents: nothing happens, because X is the lowest value. Then turn E3 one detent right. The slot reads 1/24, one twenty-fourth of a channel step between chord notes, the smallest strum division.
steps.title: First supported division

steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right, about ninety detents, through the supported divisions until the slot reads 128 channel steps, then turn a few detents further: it stays at 128 and extra turns do not go higher.
steps.title: Climb to the upper bound

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent left. The slot reads 120, the next supported division below 128; turning back left continues down towards 1/24 and X.
steps.title: One step back down
